findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === so full-day block never detected
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts line 114 checkIfIsAvailable does `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect a zero-length date override meaning unavailable all day. Dayjs objects are objects, so === is always false even when times are equal. The find callback therefore never returns true for that case, dateOverrideExist stays true, and the function later returns true meaning available. A full-day unavailable override will incorrectly show slots as bookable.

findings.title: Slot ending after date-override end is treated as available
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable only rejects a slot if slotEnd is before/same as override start or slotStart is after override end. It never checks if slotEnd is after override end. For example override 10:00-11:00 and slot 10:30-11:30 will not match either outside condition, so find returns falsy, dateOverrideExist is true and the function returns true. This allows bookings that extend past the override to be shown as available.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on same day require slot to be inside all overrides
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable uses `dateOverrides.find(date => slot is outside date)` to decide unavailable. If a day has split overrides e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00, a slot at 10:00 is inside the first but outside the second, so find matches the second and returns false. Correct logic is unavailable only if outside every override (inside none). This will incorrectly hide valid slots on split days.

findings.title: Working-hours check ignores event length and fails on split hours
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts lines 139-147 the working-hours guard computes `start` and `end` both as slotStart hour*60+minute, never adding eventLength, and uses `find` meaning any workingHours entry that does not contain the start rejects the slot. A 60-min slot starting at 17:45 with hours ending 18:00 passes even though it overruns, and a day with two intervals e.g. morning/afternoon will reject a slot valid in one interval because it is outside the other. This exposes out-of-hours slots and hides valid split-day slots.

findings.title: Date-override comparison mixes server-local and UTC timezones
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts checkIfIsAvailable builds `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset)` without utc() while slot times are `time.utc()`. dayjs(Date) renders in server local timezone, so format YYYY MM DD and isBefore/isSame/isAfter compare different zones. On a server not running UTC the day equality and boundary checks shift by the server offset, causing overrides to apply to the wrong day or allow/deny wrong slots.

findings.title: Override offset uses toString parsing and may crash on missing timezone
findings.body: In packages/lib/slots.ts lines 212-213 the code does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. toString produces a locale-dependent string with server zone abbreviation which dayjs parsing can misinterpret, and override.timeZone is optional per schedule.d.ts. If undefined, tz(undefined) can throw or return wrong offset, breaking slot generation or shifting overrides by hours/DST. It should parse the Date as UTC instant e.g. dayjs.utc(override.start).tz().

findings.title: No test for fixed-host round-robin date overrides
findings.body: The PR description claims to fix round-robin fixed-host date overrides, but apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts only adds a timezone variant of the single-user date-override test. There is no scenario with schedulingType ROUND_ROBIN plus hosts with isFixed and differing overrides, so the main fixed-host regression has no coverage and could regress silently.
